questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were ... main factors. I wanted to study in an English speaking country, I would like to go to a country, where you had the opportunity to go and explore the nature, and since I was spending a semester abroad wanted to go somewhere that I wouldn't "just" travel to due to the distance.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Both the "International Office" and "UniFlats" (the ones that organises the housing) were really quick to reply to correspondence before my departure. They had an online introduction meeting with helpful information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the online introduction meeting we had received information about how we could get to our housing, pick up our keys, etc. During the first week before classes started the "International Office" and "UniFlats" had arranged different information meetings and social events upon arrival, which was a good way to meet knew people, and get the necessary information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The majority of exchange students at Otago choose housing through UniFlats. You typically live 4-5 students in a flat (small house), where 1 is from New Zealand and the rest are study abroad/exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: All of the flats have a shared kitchen (shared between the people living there, so typically 4-5 people)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I can highly recommend UniFlats for the social aspect. It is a really great way to meet new people. We were 4 people in my flat, 2 guys and 2 girls, and we all got along really well. UniFlat also arranges a few small day trips and social arrangements (especially at the start of the semester), so it is a really great way to make friends. 
The facilities aren't always the best. Some of the houses are newly renovated (but not luxurious), while others are quite old. Some of the houses can have problems with mould, and we had to move from my first flat because of mould in the bathroom. Despite this there is no doubt that I would flat with UniFlat if I was going there again.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When choosing your courses, you're able to see the upcoming schedule for the specific courses, and in that way make sure that you don't have any overlapping courses. I had some trouble understanding the schedule at first, since you sometimes only participate in one "stream", but the "international Office" were very helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you have officially been accepted you get acces to sign up for courses. If you want to sign up for 200 or 300 level courses you have to send in documentation that you have had relevant courses prior to taking the course, but all the people that I know got their pre-requisites approved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mainly wrote with the International Office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If possible within the courses that you would like to take, try and see if you can keep either your friday (potentially monday) open. Quite a lot of exchange students do this, as it makes it easier to go on weekend trips.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one 100, one 200, and one 300 level course. I mainly found the 300 level course to be a lower level compared to 3rd year courses in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had more laboratory hours compared to my usual courses at UCPH, but on the other had we didn't have any "practice classes", where we would go over the material

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MAOR102 Māori Society
MICR223 Infection and Immunity
GENE314 Developmental Genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking MAOR102 Māori Society. For me personally it was nice to learn something about the Māori culture, how they got to New Zealand, and "their role" in society today. It is a relatively easy course with a multiple choice exam.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It wasn't really an unexpected cost, but i ended up spending quite a lot on different weekend trips.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Vegetables were more expensive than I had imagined. Especially during their winter season. 
Eating out and going out for coffee cheaper than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are quite a lot of different clubs that you can sign up for. It seemed that the most popular ones amongst exchange students where the tramping (hiking) club and the skiing club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is quite a nice gym at the university (UniPol) where you get free access, and it is relatively cheap to sign up if you wan't to join the group fitness classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
During the mid-semester break I did a tour on the South Island which I can highly recommend.

Dunedin is a great spot for going on weekend trips throughout the semester, and I would recommend going to Milford Sound and Queenstown.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. The culture in New Zealand is a lot like the Danish culture. I would say that the main difference is that people in New Zealand tend to be more "welcoming"

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you arrange your housing through UniFlats you will be living with someone from New Zealand, and are likely to meet their friends. Otherwise I found it the easiest to meet people from New Zealand in the classes where we had group projects. If you start a conversation with the locals, they're usually really nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think that there was anything i found particularly challenging, but I found it a bit odd that people are barefoot on the streets and in the grocery stores.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation for the nature. The nature in New Zealand is really beautiful, and for most people in New Zealand protecting the nature is an important part of their culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to attend the different social events in the beginning (especially the week before classes start, where you have an international orientation), as this is where it is the "easiest" to meet new people.
Try and see if you can plan some weekend trips, and explore New Zealand during the mid-semester break. 
If there is a rugby game with with New Zealand's "All Blacks" I would highly recommend trying to get tickets (even if you don't know any of the rules)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: At the Otago Polytechnic's Beauty School you can get different student led services, such as a 1 hour massage for 40 DKK.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to travel around and make memories with new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At the beginning you can feel like you're very far away from everyone you know. Both due to the distance and the time difference

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
